p.x:
HABITS is a video by @michaelcurzi. It's an engaging work of art that asks the viewer to contemplate their relationship with social media and other coping mechanisms. This analysis is my personal interpretation of the vibe. The video is linked in the next tweet.

At the start we see movement from a bed, a hand turns off a phone alarm blaring the Kanye West song Follow God:

Screamin' at my dad and he told me, "It ain't Christ-like"
But nobody never tell you when you're being like Christ
Only ever seein' me only when they-

A quick shot of a car rear-view mirror, chaotic movement in the background.

Curzi drinks coffee in a dark room, his face lit by his phone. Follow God plays again as he thumbs through a social media feed too quickly to read any of it. While driving, he brushes his teeth, trims his face and neck, and cuts his nose hair.

A sudden shot of an eye wide open, alarmed. Footage of a turbulent car crash plays, including the shot of the rear-view mirror. The music stops. Cut to black.

Another shot of Curzi in bed. The alarm plays another Kanye song, New Body:

I'll be the first one to hit your new body, oh, woah

More rapid scrolling. Back in the car, Curzi reads a book and strums a guitar while driving before the car crashes again. A third day of scrolling before more distracted driving: fast food, grooming, car crash.

The next day, Curzi has a bouquet of roses in the car. He checks his phone, looks exasperated, car crash. The next day, he tosses the bouquet away and smokes a cigarette while drinking an energy drink while eating a cake. This sequence informs my understanding of the end of the video, where he at last reaches the destination that his habits have driven him towards.

Curzi turns down the music and sits in the parked car, eyes closed, looking distraught. He looks up, gets out of the car, walks to the middle of a grassy field. He stops, his frame small in the center of the shot. He's surrounded by nature. He turns his head to look forward just before a cut to black closes the video.

Standing in the field, Curzi is alone, contemplative, seeking comfort in nature and in God. He takes in countless facsimiles of people through social media every morning but he never interacts with anyone in person. He fills his time with increasingly harmful and dangerous vices and distractions that save him from having to think about his life during his driving time.

What got him to finally reach a contemplative state? A confrontation with reality, with his loneliness. Curzi had roses in hand. A romantic gesture was imminent, but he saw something that signaled the recipient's unavailability, so he instead filled the void with a triple helping of copes. This dopamine overload at last shook him from his self-induced hypnosis and got him to step away from the perpetual distractions.

Viewers may laugh at the absurdity of the cigarette-cake-energy-drink-while-driving shots, while they themselves have habits which aren't dissimilar in their function as a distraction from their own inner or outer work. Who hasn't scrolled their phone while watching a second screen? Who hasn't drank coffee while reading just one more newsletter, one more twitter thread before they'll get started with their day?

The soundtrack reinforces Curzi's advocacy for intentional contemplation. Follow God is about Kanye's struggles to be in connection with others and to live in accordance with God's will. New Body describes a body built by plastic surgeries and the new identity built around that new body. Together, the songs and the video ask the audience: How do you see yourself? What do you live for? How are your relationships?

Overall, HABITS effectively utilizes repetition, comedy, and cinematography to present a concise story of someone coming to terms with their own destructive behaviors. Give it a watch, and try to give it your full attention when you do.

p.x:
Ep. 35: Brie Wolfson - Loving Attention & Ease in Craft

@zebriez is something of a marketing and culture wizard, and has helped some of the most incredible companies and leaders in Silicon Valley by amplifying what is true and unique about them.

That includes @cursor_ai and @mntruell, @joincolossus and @patrick_oshag, @stripe, @stripepress and @patrickc, @figma and @zoink, and others behind the scenes.

But what stands out most in Brie is her infectious joy, dedication to craft, and lifelong dance between a desire to be great and an ability to listen to and trust herself to go in unlikely directions--as she so poignantly explored in her recent essay/profile on @kevin2kelly, 'Flounder Mode.'

I hope this conversation inspires you find ways to amplify those you believe in with loving attention, settle into ease and quality in whatever you make, and pursue a life of joyful usefulness.

Available below and on all platforms.
